messages:
alex: Observing inter-region TLS failures after yesterday's RBAC sweep. ap-southeast and eu-west proxies report keystore eviction spikes starting ~2026-03-28T02:12Z. Anyone modify keystore bindings?
sec-bot: Alert: keystore.eviction spike detected (ap-southeast, eu-west) — rule KS.EvictSpike. link: https://obs.internal/alert/8600
nora: I landed infra#3099 to narrow `keystore-reader` role usage to fewer SAs. I scoped a binding to `serviceAccount:ci-bot@infra` but maybe an unintended wildcard matched.
diego: logs show KMS unwrap denies prior to TLS failure. snippet: ```
2026-03-28T02:13:05Z proxy-keystore[13]: unwrap failed: AccessDenied: Caller not authorized for cryptoKey projects/redwood/locations/eu-west/keyRings/proxy/cryptoKeys/proxy-rot
2026-03-28T02:13:05Z proxy-keystore[13]: evicting cert alias=projects/redwood/locations/eu-west/keyRings/proxy/cryptoKeys/proxy-rot
```
pak: mitigation idea: rebind `keystore-reader` for the affected cluster(s) immediately. longer-term: keystore-agent should keep active TLS certs valid for a small grace window (configurable) when KMS unwrap fails.
infra-oncall: temporary rollback applied: infra#3099-revert deployed to ap-southeast & eu-west. Keystore unwraps resumed.
alex: audit step: run KMS Audit log filter for Decrypt invocations on proxy-rot key between 02:00-02:20 UTC to ensure no unauthorized decrypts. Example: `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"`
nora: ran audit — only denies; no unexpected principals appeared. looks deny-only.
diego: risk note: if RBAC changes can cause mass evictions, customers could see increased 5xx/TLS errors. we should map detection -> incident creation. propose rule: `keystore.evictions > 10 in 5m -> create incident`.
pak: also add CI gate: when a PR touches iam bindings named `keystore*` run `keystore-sim` job which tries a decrypt using a regional SA token. fail PR on deny.
alex: security question: could a malicious RBAC change be leveraged to cause certless proxies for a takeover? If an attacker can modify IAM, they could cause evictions but would still need to get private key material elsewhere; main risk is DoS. treat unexpected keystore evictions as high-sev.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-KEYSTORE-8600 severity=medium. Runbook: https://incidents.internal/INC-KEYSTORE-8600
nora: follow-ups: SEC-701 add RBAC lint to block ambiguous IAM Conditions; INFRA-112 keystore-agent grace-cache; QA-77 keystore-sim CI job; TELE-55 alert tuning for eviction spikes.
diego: I'll open a tiny PR to make agent preserve existing cert for 120s on unwrap error and exponential backoff for refresh attempts.
pak: and I'll add the detection rule + incident auto-create mapping.
alex: thanks. let's do a 15min sync after incident ticket has logs to record timeline. (reaction :coffee:)
